title: Open the global search palette with the keyboard shortcut (K / Cmd+K)
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App.
2. You are on any page (for example the Work Orders list).
3. The persistent search field is visible in the app header and shows the shortcut hint 'Search Cmd+K'.
steps: 1. Without clicking anything, press K together with the Command key (Ctrl+K on Windows), as shown in the header search field.
expected:
1. A centered search box (a modal overlay) opens on top of the page.
2. The page behind the box is dimmed.
3. The search input is focused so you can type right away.
4. The placeholder reads a plain search placeholder (no 'ask a question' / AI wording in v1 - exact copy per the v2 design).
5. The footer keyboard legend is visible: 'Navigate' with up/down arrows, 'Select' with the enter symbol, and 'Close esc'.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.2 (Confluence page 576978945, Confluence version 12), section 5.1 Trigger and Surface; 8 Functional Requirements, read on 26 August 2026.

AUTOMATION: Not available on Build to test Yet - Last checked 8/25/2026

notes: Wording taken from design-notes (placeholder 'Search or ask a question'; footer legend). Footer legend order differs slightly between Figma captures and spec prose - VIU-confirm exact on-screen footer text once the feature is on a QA env. title: Move through result rows with the Up and Down arrow keys, skipping group headers
preconditions: 1. The palette is open and you have typed a query that returns results in more than one group (for example 'Fib' returning Work orders and Customers).
2. Results are grouped under headings such as 'Work orders (12)' and 'Customers (2)'.
steps: 1. Press the Down arrow key several times.
2. Then press the Up arrow key several times.
3. Watch which item is highlighted after each press.
expected:
1. Each Down press moves the highlight to the next result row.
2. Each Up press moves the highlight to the previous result row.
3. The highlight moves only across result rows - the group heading lines (for example 'Work orders (12)') are skipped and never get the highlight.
4. When moving down past the last row of one group, the highlight continues into the first row of the next group.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.2 (Confluence page 576978945, Confluence version 12), section 5.5 (Up/Down moves focus through visible rows, skipping group headers), read on 26 August 2026.

preconditions: 1. The palette is open with a query typed in.
